fields.label: Main heading
fields.value: Care for Anxious Patients in Fortitude Valley

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: If the thought of visiting the dentist makes your heart race, you are far from alone. Dental anxiety is common, and it can keep people away from the care they need for many years. At Precision Dental, we understand, and we will never judge you for how you feel or how long it has been since your last visit.

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: Our approach is simple: listen first, move at your pace, and give you as much control as possible over your experience.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Is Dental Anxiety?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Dental anxiety describes feelings of worry, fear or stress related to dental visits. For some people, it is mild unease. For others, it can cause a racing heart, sweaty palms, nausea or difficulty sleeping in the days before an appointment. When fear is intense enough to lead people to avoid care altogether, it is sometimes described as dental phobia.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Anxiety can stem from a painful or distressing past experience, a fear of needles, sensitivity to sounds or smells, embarrassment about the condition of your teeth, a feeling of losing control, or discomfort with someone working close to your face.

sections.label: How We Help You Feel More Comfortable

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: How We Help You Feel More Comfortable

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Time to Talk

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Your first visit can be as simple as a conversation. Tell us what worries you, and we will plan around it. There is no obligation to begin treatment until you feel ready.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Clear Explanations and Control

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We explain each step before we start and agree on a stop signal, so you can pause at any time.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Comfort Features

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Our treatment rooms have memory-foam chairs, ceiling-mounted televisions and noise-cancelling headphones. You are also welcome to bring your own music.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Happy Gas

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Happy gas, or nitrous oxide, is breathed through a small mask over your nose. It helps many people feel calm and relaxed while remaining awake and able to respond. Its effects wear off quickly after the mask is removed.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Other Sedation Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: For some patients, a prescribed oral sedative taken before an appointment may be discussed after a review of your medical history. If you choose this option, you will need someone to drive you home.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: When you book, let our team know you feel anxious so we can allow extra time. At your first visit, we start with a conversation, then carry out a gentle examination only if you are comfortable. We explain our findings clearly, prioritise any urgent concerns such as a toothache, and plan treatment in manageable steps.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Many patients find that each positive visit makes the next one easier. Keeping up regular check-ups also means concerns are found early, while treatment is usually simpler. If you had happy gas, you can usually return to normal activities shortly after your appointment, and we will let you know if any additional precautions apply.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for Anxious Patients

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for Anxious Patients

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Dr Billy Choi and our team have a genuine interest in helping nervous patients feel at ease. We take time to build trust, explain every step and never rush. Whether you need a gentle check-up or more involved care, our support is the same, from children's dentistry to adult treatment.

sections.label: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Interest-free payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Is it normal to feel anxious about the dentist?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes. Dental anxiety is very common, and there is nothing to feel embarrassed about. Letting us know helps us support you.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Will you judge me if I have not been for years?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Never. Our focus is on helping you move forward comfortably, not on how long it has been.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: What does happy gas feel like?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Many people describe a relaxed, light or tingling feeling. You remain awake and aware and can talk with us throughout.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can I drive after happy gas?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Happy gas wears off quickly, and many patients can drive after a short recovery period. We will assess you before you leave and advise you.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can I bring someone with me?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes. You are welcome to bring a support person to your appointment.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can I just have a consultation first?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Absolutely. Your first appointment can simply be a chance to meet us, talk through your concerns and see the practice before any treatment is planned.
